thesis: First Majestic is the largest primary silver producer on a major U.S. exchange, with 63% of 2026 revenue from silver across four Mexican underground mines plus its own Las Vegas bullion mint. The 2026 silver spike transformed the balance sheet: Q2 2026 revenue rose 57% YoY to $415.5M, free cash flow hit $194.6M, treasury reached a record $1,252.7M, and FY2026 guidance was raised twice to 14.6-15.5M attributable silver ounces. The stock sits 44% below its January high as silver retraced from a record $121.62/oz to ~$61/oz, leaving a debt-free producer at ~24x trailing earnings with a funded growth pipeline. The whole return depends on the silver price, and AISC inflation to $25.68/AgEq oz is eating into the margin cushion.

drivers: Silver re-accelerates to $80-100/oz as the six-year structural deficit (840M cumulative oz per management) reasserts itself; UBS has published an $80/oz target
Production lands at the top of the 14.6-15.5M attributable silver oz guidance range with 128,000-135,000 gold oz
AISC normalises back toward $22-23/AgEq oz as the Mexican peso eases and the Los Gatos rockfall and San Dimas labour disruptions stay resolved
EPS run-rate exceeds $1.50 and the market pays a mid-20s multiple on a debt-free producer with $1.2-1.3B of cash
Jerritt Canyon de-risking toward its H2 2027 restart plus the 90M oz Santo Nino and Navidad resource additions supply the growth narrative

base_case.assumptions: Silver holds a $55-70/oz band around today's ~$61/oz. AG delivers FY2026 guidance of 14.6-15.5M attributable silver ounces and 128,000-135,000 gold ounces, AISC stays in the $25-27/AgEq oz range, EPS lands near $0.90-1.10, and the stock trades at 22-25x. This range brackets the MarketBeat consensus target of ~$23.83 and sits below the TipRanks ~$25.41 average.

risks: Silver retraces to $35-40/oz as the 2026 investment-demand surge unwinds
AISC inflation does not reverse and a strong Mexican peso keeps costs elevated
The revenue-linked dividend shrinks mechanically as prices fall (Q2 declaration of $0.0152 was already below Q1's $0.0171)
Jerritt Canyon capital is spent into a weaker price environment, or the H2 2027 restart slips
Stock retests the $10.19 52-week low area on a 15-18x multiple against depressed earnings; the $1,252.7M treasury is the floor

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results — whether the $78.0M of held-back silver and gold inventory converts to revenue and whether AISC moderates from $25.68/AgEq oz
Exploration updates from the ~300 km 2026 drilling programme, including 117 km at San Dimas
FY2027 production guidance and updated exploration programme
Targeted Jerritt Canyon gold mine restart in Nevada after $75M of 2026 investment, new owner-operated fleet and mill modernisation
Santa Elena mill expansion to 3,500 tpd from ~3,100 tpd delivering incremental output from Santo Nino and Navidad
Silver price direction — each $10/oz move is worth on the order of $150M+ of annualised pre-tax cash flow; the dividend is set at 2% of net quarterly revenue and tracks price mechanically

key_risks: Silver price is the entire thesis — the metal fell from a record $121.62/oz on 29 January 2026 to ~$61/oz by late September, and AG's earnings, dividend and multiple all move with it
Cost inflation is partly structural — AISC rose 22% YoY to $25.68/AgEq oz on a stronger peso, higher royalties, production taxes and worker-participation costs that scale with metal prices

Consecutive consensus misses — Q2 2026 came in at $0.21 adjusted EPS versus $0.25 expected and $415.5M revenue versus ~$496M forecast, as concentrate mark-to-market and inventory timing make quarters hard to model
Execution risk on the Jerritt Canyon restart — a mine suspended since March 2023, restarting with a new fleet and a self-perform mining model

Single-jurisdiction concentration — all four producing mines are in Mexico, exposing the company to mining-law reform, tax disputes (a $10.1M one-time charge settled a historic dispute in Q2 2026), permitting and community relations
Operational fragility — the Los Gatos main-ramp rockfall and San Dimas labour disruption both hit a single quarter
The dividend is not a floor — at 2% of revenue it falls automatically with prices, and the ~0.3% yield offers no income support
